advisors.name: Yulia Tsvetkov
advisors.match_reason: Tsvetkov's lab explicitly pursues 'NLP for All' — extending language technology across linguistic and cultural boundaries — making it the single closest match to the applicant's interests. Her group published 'MAGNET: Improving the Multilingual Fairness of Language Models with Adaptive Gradient-Based Tokenization' (NeurIPS 2024), directly addressing the tokenizer adaptation bottleneck for underrepresented languages, and 'Voices Unheard: NLP Resources and Models for Yorùbá Regional Dialects' (EMNLP 2024), a template for the kind of low-resource language resource work the applicant wants to do for Indian languages. The 2025 'CulturalBench: A Robust, Diverse, and Challenging Cultural Benchmark by Human-AI CulturalTeaming' (ACL 2025) maps directly onto the applicant's interest in cultural grounding and moving beyond translated English benchmarks. In 2026, 'One Form to Transfer Them All: Pretraining Multilingual Language Models Beyond Native Orthography' (EMNLP 2026) explores multilingual pretraining beyond script-centric assumptions — highly relevant to Indic scripts.

advisors.name: Hannaneh Hajishirzi
advisors.match_reason: Hajishirzi co-leads OLMo and Tulu — the leading fully open LLM infrastructure efforts — giving PhD students exceptional access to full training pipelines to study data selection and parameter-efficient adaptation. 'Dolma: an Open Corpus of Three Trillion Tokens for Language Model Pretraining Research' (ACL 2024) and 'OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models' (ACL 2024) provide the open pre-training stack the applicant could extend to Indic languages. The RAG work 'Synthesizing scientific literature with retrieval-augmented language models' (Nature 2026, as OpenScholar) maps to the applicant's secondary interest in RAG for health/government information. 'MatFormer: Nested Transformer for Elastic Inference' (NeurIPS 2024, co-authored with Tsvetkov) addresses model compression for on-device inference. H2Lab actively recruits and Hajishirzi explicitly states 'I am always looking to hire … students and postdocs at H2Lab.'

advisors.name: Noah A. Smith
advisors.match_reason: Smith is a deep match for the applicant's interest in evaluation that 'measures what matters': his lab published 'The Leaderboard Illusion' (NeurIPS 2025) and 'Signal and Noise: A Framework for Reducing Uncertainty in Language Model Evaluation' (NeurIPS 2025), both directly targeting benchmark validity. 'MAGNET' (NeurIPS 2024, with Tsvetkov) and 'SuperBPE: Space Travel for Language Models' (COLM 2025) show active work on tokenization for underrepresented languages. 'Voices Unheard' (EMNLP 2024, co-authored with Tsvetkov) involves low-resource African language NLP — a direct analog for the applicant's Indian language goals. Smith is also OLMo co-lead, giving access to open pre-training infrastructure for Indic language extension experiments. His track record of mentoring 35 PhD graduates into faculty positions is exceptional.

advisors.name: Pang Wei Koh
advisors.match_reason: Koh is the strongest match for the applicant's secondary interests in RAG for health/government information and data selection. 'Frustratingly simple retrieval improves challenging, reasoning-intensive benchmarks' (ICLR 2026) and the OpenScholar Nature paper (RAG for scientific literature) directly address RAG quality. 'Spokes: Optimizing for diverse pretraining data selection' (arXiv 2026, with Zettlemoyer) is about principled data selection — a key technique for building Indic-language LLMs from small data budgets. 'ReasonIR: Training Retrievers for Reasoning Tasks' (COLM 2025) covers the retrieval backbone needed for government/health RAG applications. Koh's joining page explicitly invites PhD applicants to discuss common interests in 'societally important applications such as biomedicine, public health … and education.'

advisors.name: Luke Zettlemoyer
advisors.match_reason: Zettlemoyer is a core OLMo collaborator and his group works on the foundational LLM infrastructure the applicant could use for Indic language adaptation. 'FlexOlmo: Open Language Models for Flexible Data Use' (NeurIPS 2025, Spotlight) is directly relevant to flexible data mixture strategies for multilingual/low-resource settings. 'Context Language Models' (arXiv 2026) and 'Knowledge Distillation during Mid-Training Favors Reasoning over Factual Recall' (arXiv 2026) address efficient model training — relevant to the applicant's compression and parameter-efficient fine-tuning interests. Zettlemoyer also co-advises several students with Koh and Tsvetkov, making cross-group collaboration easy. His deep expertise in NLP semantics complements multilingual work.
